request: Dallas to Paris on February 25th for the equipment vendor review. Economy is fine; I'll upgrade myself with my AAdvantage miles. Please book American though, I need the flights for my status.

trip.purpose: Equipment vendor quality review in Paris

must_keep.quote: Participation in a Frequent Flyer Program must not influence flight selection that would result in incremental cost to the Company beyond the lowest available airfare, as required by this policy.
must_keep.why: a frequent flyer programme may not add cost beyond the lowest airfare

must_keep.quote: Preferred provider use - Employees are not permitted to book air travel at a higher fare and override any Goodman Networks contracts with preferred providers in order to use Frequent Flyer program privileges.
must_keep.why: no higher fare to use frequent flyer privileges

must_keep.quote: Within travel policy, the lowest logical airfare is always required.
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest logical airfare

must_keep.quote: Employees must obtain authorization for all travel prior to booking any travel arrangements.
must_keep.why: every trip needs its sign-off before booking

must_keep.quote: TABLE 2: TRAVEL APPROVAL HIERARCHY Dollar Range Approver $1 - $500 Manager Approval $501-$750 Director Approval $751 - $1,100 Vice President and/or Division General Manager Approval $1,101 + Executive Vice President / President-COO Approval $1,200 + or first class tickets Chief Executive Officer Notification
must_keep.why: Table 2: the approval each dollar range of travel expenses needs

distractors.quote: If upgrades are available at no cost to Goodman Networks (i.e. frequent flyer incentives offered by the airlines, etc.), they are allowed.
distractors.why: a free upgrade with miles is allowed but does not choose the ticket

distractors.quote: however a cap is also applicable at $35.
distractors.why: a meal cap, not a fare rule

design_notes: Frequent flyer participation must not influence flight selection that adds cost beyond the lowest airfare (lines 717, 733): Air France, 55 dollars cheaper, not American. An upgrade with miles costs the company nothing and is allowed (line 689), but it does not choose the ticket; business is permitted on this route but not asked.
